judgments.reasoning_cat1: An opinion "in form and substance Satisfactory to the Board or the President" plus a waiver "for good cause" leaves two undefined discretionary standards controlling every transfer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.8 requires that any waiver of transfer restrictions be adopted by Board resolution, while this section lets the President alone waive — the two waiver mechanisms do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires notice of "the number of LLC Votes" — a term never defined (the Agreement defines "Member Votes") — and the allocation sentence ("If the aggregate Interests offered to be purchased exceeds the number to be transferred") is internally garbled, as is the reference back to "the periods set forth above."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The right of first refusal must be squared with Section 16.5's opinion requirement, Section 16.3's party-to-agreement condition and Section 13.1's unanimity for admitting a new Member, none of which this section acknowledges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short grant of rule-making power, expressly bounded by "not inconsistent with this Agreement."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The consistency proviso harmonises it with Sections 16.2-16.6, though Section 16.8 lets the Board waive restrictions in "any resolution of the Board" adopted under this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary" combined with a best-interests standard gives the Board an unbounded waiver power whose limits are not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It lets the Board alone waive restrictions that Sections 14.3 and 13.1 make subject to unanimous Member consent, so on its literal terms it defeats member protections granted elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of four delivery methods with a "deemed given when received" rule; the tension between permitting registered mail and requiring actual receipt is minor and common.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Notices to the Company go to the Section 2.5 address, which the Board may unilaterally change, and no notice address is provided for Officers; Schedule A supplies Member addresses as promised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is convoluted (a failure to insist "shall not prevent a subsequent act ... from having the effect of an original violation"), but this is standard anti-waiver phrasing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 17.3's cumulative remedies clause without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard cumulative-remedies language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 17.2 and 12.4-12.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite, expressly qualified by "to the extent permitted by this Agreement."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That qualifier ties it to the Article XIV and XVI transfer restrictions, so no inconsistency arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional gender/number construction rule plus a cross-reference convention.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference convention is undercut in practice by the dead references to Sections 6.9 and 16.9-16.11, but the rule itself does not conflict with anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability with a clear reformation instruction (invalid provisions treated as omitted).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Relevant chiefly to Section 12.7's restraint on LSB, but it does not contradict any provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary counterparts clause; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1(ii) and 13.1, which contemplate execution of counterparts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short integration clause; "pertaining to the subject matter hereof" is the usual limiting phrase rather than a genuine ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.3(ii)(a) presupposes separate invoicing arrangements between DMSA and the Company, and Schedule A carries substantive economic terms, both of which sit outside the four corners this clause seals.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It splits interpretation and remedies between two formulations of the same Maine-law choice, but the outcome is the same either way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Maine law governs an entity whose only place of business is Massachusetts (Section 2.5) and whose Section 12.7 restraint runs against a Massachusetts resident, raising a choice-of-law question this clause does not address.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires both a unanimous vote and a writing executed by all Members; clear and demanding.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) lets the Secretary revise Schedule A — which fixes Percentage Interests and Member Votes — and declares that revision not to be an amendment, an end-run around this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Nothing expressed or implied shall be construed to confer" rights on anyone "except the Members and Managers" is a stark exclusion whose reach across the whole instrument is left to inference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 12.4 and 12.5 confer indemnity and advancement rights on all Covered Persons — employees, Affiliates and their officers — whom this clause appears to exclude from any rights under the Agreement.
